subject: Convergence plan & technical parity checklist — follow-up
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena@helixcare.com>
To: Soo Jin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Bryan Chen <bryan@helixcare.com>
Date: 2026-09-21T15:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Intro / HelixCare evaluation — follow-up and asks

Soojin — thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap from our side and a couple of clarifying questions before we lock the bakeoff scope.

Top pain points (priority order):
- Predictable 95th pct latency for short, multi-turn clinical prompts (under 220ms target).
- Unit cost per generated token for our triage flows (we budget tightly).
- Auditability: immutable request logs, KV cache handling, and retention controls for compliance.
- Multi-cloud parity: we run EU workloads in GCP and US in AWS; any variance in latency/perf matters.

Competitor note: Vendor X is showing strong cold-start throughput on our baseline tests but their output hallucination rate on structured extraction is concerning. We want head-to-head parity on the extraction task.

What we need from Redwood to proceed to a bakeoff:
1) An explicit test plan we can run in our environment (or with a short-term sandbox) that covers: latency percentiles (P50/P95), cold vs warmed KV-cache behavior, token cost estimate for our sample traces, and a quality extraction sweep against our annotated dataset.
2) A short timeline (2–3 weeks preferred) and a matrix of what Redwood needs from us (sample data, auth, IP allowlist, sandbox creds).
3) Any known model variants you recommend for cost vs quality tradeoffs for extraction workloads.

I've attached our itemized bakeoff asks. Happy to jump on a quick sync if needed — Bryan and I are available Tue/Wed afternoons PT.

—Elena
Director, Product — HelixCare

Attachments: helixcare-itemized-bakeoff-asks.pdf
From: Soo Jin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@helixcare.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-21T18:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Intro / HelixCare evaluation — convergence plan + proposed tests

Elena — great notes, thanks for laying this out clearly. Below is a concise post-call recap and our proposed bakeoff playbook. I’ve looped Camila (solutions) and Marissa (competitive/pricing) to own test design and commercial framing.

Key alignment (we heard):
- Primary success metric: P95 latency <= 220ms on short clinical prompts while preserving extraction F1 >= HelixCare baseline.
- Cost ceiling: target per-session cost that keeps triage flows within your budget constraints (you provided sample traces in the PDF).
- Compliance requirements: request-level audit logs retained for 365 days, exportable.
- Multi-cloud parity must be demonstrated (GCP vs AWS).

Proposed bakeoff tests (short — 10-day sprint):
1) Latency sweep (P50/P95/P99) on your short-turn prompts, run in both regions; report warm vs cold starts. Owner: Camila.
2) KV-cache behavior: measure first-request vs warmed-KV throughput and token delta using your annotated traces. Owner: Camila.
3) Extraction quality sweep: run 1k annotated samples, produce F1/precision/recall vs your baseline and Vendor X. Owner: Camila + HelixCare data team.
4) Cost projection: run a 100-session simulated run to estimate per-session token consumption and projected monthly cost. Owner: Marissa.
5) Ops & auditability check: demonstrate log export, retention config, and an example audit extract. Owner: Soo Jin.

Deliverables we’ll provide in the drive folder: interop-test-plan.xlsx (test matrix + schedules), redwood-bakeoff-scorecard.csv (template for results), and a short runbook for sandbox access. Ask from HelixCare: a 1k-sample extract (anonymized) and an allowlist for test IPs.

Timing: if we start Monday 2026-09-27, we can deliver results by Friday 2026-10-08 (10 business days). If that works, I’ll schedule three short checkpoints (kickoff, mid-sprint check, readout).

Open questions for HelixCare:
- Do you prefer Redwood to run tests in your GCP project or in our reserved sandbox with network peering?
- Any regulatory constraints on uploading the 1k annotated samples to our sandbox?

Next steps: Elena, if you confirm sandbox choice and share the anonymized samples + allowlist, Camila will publish the detailed schedule by EOD Monday.

Thanks — looking forward to running this.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: interop-test-plan.xlsx, redwood-bakeoff-scorecard.csv
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Soo Jin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-22T01:15:00Z
Subject: Re: Convergence plan + tactical test notes

Looping in a few tactical clarifications from the test-design perspective. Quick points:

- Test harness: I’ll reuse our in-house runner but need HelixCare’s sample schema and a lightweight adapter (JSON sample mapping). Can adapt in ~2 days.
- Latency measurement: we’ll capture P50/P95/P99 via synthetic arrival patterns and also replay real trace timestamps so cold-start behavior is realistic. For cold starts, plan >= 30s idle gap to replicate lambda-like conditions.
- KV-cache probe: include a warm vs cold run for the same 100 prompts and measure token delta and latency. Add a request-level trace ID for audit correlation.
- Quality: will run extraction through the same evaluation harness we use internally and output both per-example and aggregate results (F1, precision, recall, example-level failure cases).
- Thresholds: propose we flag parity if F1 is within -3 points of HelixCare baseline OR absolute F1 >= 0.86 (whichever is higher).

Commercial ask (Marissa) — I recommend we prepare two pricing scenarios: a conservative committed rate for Dedicated (if they want predictable cost) and a usage-based estimate to show tradeoffs during the POC. Marissa, can you own the numbers?

I’ll draft the runnable scripts and push the interop-test-plan.xlsx to the shared drive by Monday morning.

—Camila
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
